Hi Karthik / Grace,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the event triage. Our forensics team pulled a set of packet captures and session logs during the window (attached: pcap-snapshot-20250913.zip). Before we proceed with any export from Redwood's side we need to confirm:

1) How long will Redwood retain the unredacted forensic artifacts by default?
2) Who at Redwood has the authority to approve permanent deletion once our internal investigation completes?
3) Are there regional residency constraints or export steps we need to follow for data that includes EU-origin sessions? (This particular customer traffic is US-only, but we want to know the policy.)

We may need the artifacts retained for up to ~120 days depending on regulators, but we'd prefer to formalize the retention window and deletion authority now. Please advise next steps and any internal request form you need us to complete.

Thanks,
Linda Santos
Security Operations Lead
Acme Corporation
linda.santos@acmeco.com

Subject: Re: Packet captures + timeline — retention question

Linda — thanks for the context and for the artifact. High level answers below, plus proposed next steps.

Short answers:
- Default temporary hold for incident artifacts: 90 days from the date Redwood ingests/export-stage of the evidence.
- Deletion authority: Redwood requires a joint sign-off — Customer PO/SEC lead + Redwood Legal or Security Manager. For permanent deletion we require a signed request form that lists the artifacts, scope, and deletion date.
- Regional constraints: Redwood honors data residency flags. If artifacts contain EU-origin data, we will store/route the evidence to the EU evidence vault and follow EU retention guidance unless customer authorizes cross-border export. Since you note this traffic is US-only, default US handling applies.

Proposed path forward:
1) If Acme wants a 90-day hold, reply to this thread authorizing Redwood to retain the artifacts for 90 days (we will mark a hold in our Evidence Tracking system).
2) Complete the attached Redwood IR evidence request form (we'll accept the drive link or a signed PDF).
3) We will produce a chain-of-custody CSV and SHA256 checksums for the exported bundles and share them with your team within 24 hours of export.
4) If you anticipate >90 days (e.g., 120 or 180), please state that explicitly and include the regulatory justification so we can route to Legal for exception approval.

I'll schedule a short sync if helpful. We can also provide a cost estimate for long-term cold storage if you prefer Redwood to continue holding beyond the default window.

Next steps: Linda — please confirm the hold length and attach the signed request (or point to your internal ticket).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Security Accounts
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: forensic extraction retention windows & deletion authority

Thanks for the thread — a couple of legal notes to make the process clean: 

- Deletion / destruction of forensic evidence: Redwood requires written authorization from the customer security or legal lead plus a Redwood Legal representative. We maintain a documented approval chain for auditability.
- Exceptions: We can approve extensions up to 180 days internally for regions where regulators typically request more time, but exceptions beyond 180 days will need external counsel sign-off and a written justification.
- Evidence slicing: We recommend providing a scoped list of sessions/IDs to limit PII exposure. If Acme provides session identifiers we will produce a sliced export and a redaction report.

Attached is our IR evidence request template (IR_evidence-request-form.pdf) — please complete the sections that identify artifacts, desired retention window, and deletion authority. Once we receive a completed form we will create a formal evidence hold (and produce the chain-of-custody manifest).

Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
